preconditions.description: Number of test cases T is between 1 and 3.
Number of old cities K and total cities N satisfy 2 <= K <= N <= 10^5.
Number of newer roads M satisfies 0 <= M <= 10^5.
Starting city S is between 1 and N.
Length of roads between old cities X is between 1 and 10^9.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= a_i <= N and 1 <= b_i <= N and 1 <= c_i <= 10**9 for a_i, b_i, c_i in roads)
preconditions.description: Each road connects cities a_i and b_i with length c_i, where 1 <= a_i, b_i <= N and 1 <= c_i <= 10^9.

preconditions.expression: all(a_i != b_i for a_i, b_i, _ in roads)
preconditions.description: No road connects a city to itself.

preconditions.expression: len(set((a_i, b_i) for a_i, b_i, _ in roads)) == len(roads)
all(any(dijkstra(S, i) < float('inf') for i in range(1, N+1))
preconditions.description: It's possible to get from every city to every other city using one or more roads.

postconditions.description: The number of output lines equals the number of test cases T.

postconditions.expression: all(len(distances) == N for distances in output)
postconditions.description: Each output line contains N integers representing distances from city S to each city.
The distance from city S to itself is 0.

postconditions.expression: all(distances[i] >= 0 for distances in output for i in range(N))
